Frequently Asked Questions

1. How do I open RedactLocal on macOS Sequoia / Sonoma?
Because RedactLocal is an independent open-source utility operating 100% offline (no Apple cloud notary telemetry), macOS may show an alert: "Apple could not verify RedactLocal is free of malware".
Fix (Takes 3 seconds):
1. On the alert, click Done.
2. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security and scroll down to the Security section.
3. Click "Open Anyway" and enter your password or Touch ID.
Or run in Terminal: xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ~/Downloads/RedactLocal*.dmg
2. Does the Free Web Scanner upload my documents to any server?
Zero bytes are ever uploaded. The Free Web Triage Scanner is compiled into WebAssembly and runs in private browser RAM on your local CPU. You can disconnect your Wi-Fi or turn on Airplane mode and the scanner will continue to audit documents in real-time.
3. Why do black rectangles drawn in Acrobat or Preview fail in court?
Everyday PDF editors only superimpose an opaque black box on layer 5. The underlying character glyph bytecodes (Tj/TJ) and interactive form fields (/V) remain completely intact inside the file. Anyone who drags their mouse and hits Cmd+C can paste the hidden secrets into a text editor. RedactLocal permanently deletes the bytecodes from the file stream.
4. How does the offline Founders Pass license work?
RedactLocal uses asymmetric Ed25519 digital cryptography. When you purchase a license, you receive a tamper-evident .rlkey file. The desktop application validates the digital signature locally on your machine with zero remote authentication calls.
